transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi there! Do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can go back to light exercise, such as gardening, one week after surgery. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for that information. I also wanted to know, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's good to know. Another thing—I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside. However, if you have significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, that is not normal and we may need to assess this further. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
